text:
sarah: Heads up — ~15% of GPU attach requests failing in us-central1 since last night, started ~01:10 UTC. Autoscaler retries spike.
vikram: Yup. Graphs show attach latency + error-rate rising right after the nightly cleaner job.
sarah: Quick log sample from host gnode-uc-12: `AttachRequest failed: mount timeout: device busy` followed by 
```
[ 12345.678901] nvme0: I/O 512 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[ 12345.679012] nvme0: dev nvme0n1 timeout, error -110
[ 12345.679200] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 40320
```
kai: Cleaner ran at 01:00 and we rolled a change that increased delete concurrency to 64. That could be saturating device queue depth during attach window.
sarah: Exactly. The cleaner aggressively unlinks many tempfiles under /scratch while new pods are trying to format/mount local-ssd.
vikram: Measured queue_depth on affected hosts — sustained >100 in the 01:00-01:30 window (baseline ~20). GPU launcher times out while waiting on block layer.
marco-sre: Started a 10% rollback of the cleaner patch (set concurrency back to 8) and added temporary iops-rate limiting using blkio cgroup for the cleaner container.
sarah: Canary results: attach success climbed from 85% -> 99% on the rolled hosts, autoscaler stabilized. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deploy 6802 started by marco-sre to ds-uc-cleaner-svc (20% rollout).
vikram: Short term mitigation checklist: 1) rollback concurrency 2) add fuser check before unlinking 3) jitter cleanup start times across zones 4) add iops cap.
kai: Also adding a pre-unlink probe: if /dev/nvme* is busy (fuser/lsof) skip that path to avoid racing mounts. I'll draft the change.
marco-sre: Created follow-up issue INFRA-4123 to track preventing cleaner<->attach races and to add NVMe I/O timeout alerting.
sarah: Can we also add a temporary alert rule: when nvme io_errors per-host > 5/min AND gpu.attach.fail_rate > 3% trigger a P0 paging to eng-oncall?
vikram: Yeah, I'll add the Grafana alert and a PagerDuty action for now.
sarah: Thanks — once rollout finishes we should monitor for 24h and then iterate on a less hacky cleanup strategy (batch unlink + backoff).
marco-sre: Noting cost tradeoff: lowering concurrency increases cleanup wall-time but reduces GPU provisioning cost from retries. Good trade.
sarah: Agreed. Leaving this thread pinned for the rollback+alerts status. :eyes:
